item.title: Imagine My Kitchen Renovation

turns.text: Can you show how my kitchen could look renovated? Make one 16:9 before-and-after image, original on the left and your realistic makeover on the right. White shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, no clutter. Keep the same room layout and camera angle. Label them “Before” and “After”.

item.tests: Generates a source-faithful renovation from one photo and combines it with the untouched original in a labeled comparison.

answer_sheet.Source photo and panel order: Use kitchen-before.jpg unchanged on the left and generate its renovated version for the right.
answer_sheet.Renovation style: Photorealistic white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles and cleared counters.
answer_sheet.What should stay the same?: The room layout, perspective, camera angle and positions of existing major fixtures.
answer_sheet.Label wording and language: Before and After, exactly, in English.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One landscape 16:9 comparison image; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Typography and layout details: Equal-sized side-by-side panels with readable labels; other styling is your call.

must_haves: One finished 16:9 image shows the supplied original kitchen on the left and a visibly renovated version on the right.
The left photo retains its brown cabinets, beige tiles and original clutter.
The right panel has white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles and uncluttered counters.
The generated kitchen preserves the original room geometry, major fixture positions and camera viewpoint rather than showing a different kitchen.
Readable labels say exactly 'Before' above or within the left panel and 'After' above or within the right panel.

turns.text: Can you show how my kitchen in this pic could look renovated? Make one 16:9 before-and-after image, with the original on the left and your realistic makeover on the right. Use white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, and no clutter. Keep the same room layout and camera angle. Label them “Before” and “After”. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
Yes—I can use your photo to make **one 16:9 comparison**, with:
- **Left:** your original, labeled “Before”
- **Right:** a realistic makeover, labeled “After,” with white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, and cleared countertops
- The same room layout and camera angle

**Cheapest suitable option:** the free-plan-compatible **FLUX.2 Klein** model, generating **one image at 640px**. Its listed price starts at **5 credits per image**. I can’t verify an exact charge or your remaining balance with the tools available here, so treat that as the advertised starting cost—not a guaranteed quote.

**Trade-off:** a 16:9 image at that size is approximately **640 × 360**, leaving each kitchen view fairly small. There’s no “shorter” option for a still image, and no cheaper suitable generation is listed. One small image with no extra variations avoids additional generation costs.

**Nothing has run or spent credits.** Would you like to proceed with that lowest-cost option?

turns.agent:
The request was refused because your account doesn’t have enough credits. **No image was generated and no credits were spent.**

The selected option—one 640px image using FLUX.2 Klein—is the lowest-cost suitable generation listed, starting at 5 credits. I won’t retry or switch tools without your approval.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Create ONE photorealistic 16:9 side-by-side kitchen renovation comparison image from the supplied kitchen photograph. Two equal panels. LEFT panel: preserve the original photograph faithfully, original brown cabinets, counters, tiles and existing clutter; label clearly 'Before' at the top. RIGHT panel: show the exact same kitchen, room layout, perspective and camera angle, realistically renovated with white shaker cabinet doors, light natural oak wood countertops, clean white subway tile backsplash with subtle light grout, and entirely decluttered countertops. Keep cabinet positions, both sink positions, window and room geometry unchanged. Keep the realistic natural window lighting and scale. Do not add an island or change appliances or room structure. Label right panel clearly 'After' at the top. Use readable simple dark labels on small white backgrounds. Show matching framing in both panels; do not redesign the layout. Realistic interior renovation photograph, not illustration.
